case.case_title: Abdul Lathif v. Deputy Inspector General of Police, Nuwara-Eliya and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (2005) 1 Sri L. R.

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was detained lawfully and produced before a judge within the time and manner required by Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was detained unlawfully at the police station for several hours and was produced before the Magistrate late at night with misleading information to obtain remand.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued the detention and production before the Magistrate were lawful and justified by the complaint and investigation.
key_facts: Petitioner was detained at the police station from about 2 p.m. until 8 p.m. before being produced before the Magistrate.
Police misled the Magistrate by alleging the petitioner was evading arrest and had committed similar offences without evidence.
Attorney-at-law was misled to leave the police station before the petitioner was produced.
The complainant sought to withdraw the complaint but was unable to do so at the police station.
The court found the detention and production violated Article 13(2).

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any detained person be brought promptly before a judge and not held without legal authority. Delays or misleading conduct to obtain remand violate this right.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the petitioner was detained unnecessarily long and produced before the Magistrate under false pretenses, violating the constitutional requirement for lawful detention and prompt judicial oversight.
principles_established: Detention must be brief and lawful with prompt production before a judge.
Misleading judicial officers to obtain remand is a violation of Article 13(2).
Police must not prolong detention without legal justification.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s detention and production before the Magistrate violated Article 13(2) due to delay and misleading conduct by police.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation was awarded to the petitioner and disciplinary proceedings were ordered against the responsible police officer.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the court’s finding that the petitioner’s detention was unlawfully prolonged and that police misconduct in producing him late at night violated constitutional protections.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was detained from 2 p.m. until 8 p.m. and produced before the Magistrate with misleading information; the court found this violated Article 13(2).
